neighbours.label: a plant or crop spreading, multiplying or flourishing (growth verbs in gardening text)
fire: In moist shade the fern spreads steadily and multiplies through underground rhizomes.
Given full sun and rich soil, the young apple trees flourish and fruit within three years.
Mint propagates aggressively, so the clump doubles in size every season.
After the rains the wildflowers proliferate across the hillside and self-seed freely.
Strawberry plants multiply by sending out runners that root wherever they touch the soil.
Once established, the bamboo thrives and colonises the whole border within a few years.
The bulbs naturalise easily and multiply into large drifts after several springs.
In warm water the duckweed flourishes and quickly covers the surface of the pond.
quiet: In moist shade the fern looks dark green, and its fronds are about a foot long.
Given full sun and rich soil, the young apple trees were pruned and labelled in spring.
Mint has a strong smell, so the clump is planted near the kitchen door.
After the rains the wildflowers were photographed by a group of students from town.
Strawberry plants are sold in small pots at the market for two dollars each.
Once delivered, the bamboo canes are stacked against the shed until we need them.
The bulbs are stored in paper bags in the garage until autumn.
In warm water the duckweed is easy to scoop out with a net.
